title: Man-Made Heuristics Are Dead. Long Live Code Generators!

mechanism.domainTask: Context-specific cache eviction and Linux TCP congestion-control heuristic synthesis
mechanism.populationDetail: Each round generates a batch of 25 independent heuristics; top candidates are drawn from the undivided history, with no islands or tree structure.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The two highest-performing heuristics across all previous caching rounds are retained as examples for the next round.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The top-two reusable example set is explicit, but the paper does not specify the persistent storage or retention of non-elite candidates; congestion control reports 100 candidate attempts without a separate update policy.
mechanism.generationDetail: The LLM synthesizes the heuristic body within a fixed template/interface; prior high-performing heuristics are examples rather than code explicitly edited as parents.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Numeric miss-rate/performance scores guide ranking; compiler stderr and verifier pass/fail are provided to the Generator for correction after invalid output.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: No true editable parent is selected. The global top two prior cache policies are selected by performance rank as contextual examples; the rule for selecting the initial LRU/LFU seed examples is fixed.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Man-Made Heuristics Are Dead. Long Live CodeGenerators!.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The current survey cites PolicySmith under Rank-Based Selection. In the described prompt workflow the top-two ranked programs are contextual examples, not true editable parents; retain or revise that citation with this distinction made clear. The paper also merits coverage in population, multi-elite archive, replacement, candidate-prompt/from-scratch generation, single-model, metadata, staged-evaluation, and implicit-control discussions, where it is currently not cited.
